answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The kernel multiplier is published, charged in ivory, and nectar lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3971 identities would post 1267 proofs and burn roughly 66 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
